ANA.name: Anaheim Ducks
text: The Ducks are 11-11-1 so far.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
Night to night, they give up dangerous chances and rarely get burned after losing the puck.
Their goaltending has let them down.

BOS.name: Boston Bruins
text: The Bruins are 14-7-1 so far.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 14 of their 22 games.
Night to night, they leave most of the shooting to the forwards and sit back rather than forecheck.
Their goaltending has been stealing games, but they spend a lot of time in the box.

BUF.name: Buffalo Sabres
text: The Sabres are 9-9-4 so far.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Their game? They rarely get stuck out on long shifts and rarely block shots.

CGY.name: Calgary Flames
text: The Flames are 10-12-1, still looking for their first playoff spot in four seasons.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
Night to night, they fire from everywhere, though a lot of it is hopeful and get caught after turnovers too often.
Their power play has no bite and they spend a lot of time in the box.

CAR.name: Carolina Hurricanes
text: The defending champs are picking up right where they left off, 16-3-3 out of the gate.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 19 of their 22 games.
Expect them to spend most of the night in the other team’s end and give up dangerous chances.
They create chances even when shorthanded and their penalty kill is airtight.

CHI.name: Chicago Blackhawks
text: The rebuild grinds on in Chicago: no playoffs in six seasons, and a 6-14-2 start.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Their game? They spend a lot of the night in their own end and rarely block shots.
Their power play has no bite.

COL.name: Colorado Avalanche
text: Same old Avalanche: 13-7-3, and in the mix again.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they shoot from distance and play fast, wide-open games.
Their penalty kill is airtight and they stay out of the box.

CBJ.name: Columbus Blue Jackets
text: The rebuild grinds on in Columbus: no playoffs in six seasons, and a 8-12-0 start.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
On the ice, they send their defensemen in to shoot and shoot from distance.

DAL.name: Dallas Stars
text: The Stars are 14-6-2, which is what we’ve come to expect, winners of four straight.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
On the ice, they get in front of a lot of shots and grind games down.
Their penalty kill is airtight, but they spend a lot of time in the box.

DET.name: Detroit Red Wings
text: The rebuild grinds on in Detroit: no playoffs in ten seasons, and a 8-11-3 start.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
Night to night, they get in front of a lot of shots and ice the puck a lot to get out of trouble.
Their penalty kill leaks.

EDM.name: Edmonton Oilers
text: The Oilers are 17-4-3, which is what we’ve come to expect.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they lean hard on their top players and grind games down.
Their power play is lethal.

FLA.name: Florida Panthers
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Panthers are 12-8-3.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they hound the puck in the other team’s end and get into a lot of chippy games.
Their power play is lethal and their penalty kill is airtight.

LAK.name: Los Angeles Kings
text: The Kings have made the playoffs five years running, but they’re 7-11-2 this time.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
Expect them to keep the other team to hopeful shots and leave most of the shooting to the forwards.

MIN.name: Minnesota Wild
text: The Wild are 17-3-4 so far, winners of five straight.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 13 of their 24 games.
Night to night, they get pinned in their own end on long shifts and crash the net for second chances.
Their goaltending has been stealing games and they stay out of the box.

MTL.name: Montréal Canadiens
text: The Canadiens are 14-5-4 so far.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
On the ice, they get into a lot of chippy games and give up dangerous chances.
They spend a lot of time in the box, but their goaltending has been stealing games.

NSH.name: Nashville Predators
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Predators have bounced back to 11-6-5.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they get pinned in their own end on long shifts and keep things calm after the whistle.

NJD.name: New Jersey Devils
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Devils have bounced back to 15-7-0.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 16 of their 22 games.
Night to night, they play a finesse game and pounce on turnovers.
They stay out of the box and their power play is lethal.

NYI.name: New York Islanders
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Islanders are 10-6-5.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they send their defensemen in to shoot and get caught after turnovers too often.
Their goaltending has been stealing games, but their power play has no bite.

NYR.name: New York Rangers
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Rangers have bounced back to 13-8-1, winners of three straight.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they get a lot of their shots blocked and get right to the net.

OTT.name: Ottawa Senators
text: The Senators are 14-6-3 so far.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 15 of their 23 games.
Night to night, they rarely get burned after losing the puck and rarely get stuck out on long shifts.
Their goaltending has let them down.

PHI.name: Philadelphia Flyers
text: The Flyers are 8-11-6 so far.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Their game? They grind games down and push out to take away the point shot.

PIT.name: Pittsburgh Penguins
text: The Penguins are 7-12-2 so far.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
Their game? They get right to the net and sit back rather than forecheck.
Their power play has no bite.

SJS.name: San Jose Sharks
text: The Sharks are 10-12-2, still looking for their first playoff spot in seven seasons.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
Their game? They ice the puck a lot to get out of trouble and shoot from distance.
Their power play has no bite and their penalty kill leaks.

SEA.name: Seattle Kraken
text: The Kraken are 10-8-1, still looking for their first playoff spot in three seasons.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
Expect them to let the other team shoot, but mostly hopeful shots and find a way to get their shots past the blockers.
Their penalty kill leaks.

STL.name: St. Louis Blues
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Blues are 11-9-2.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they keep things calm after the whistle and get to the dangerous chances.

TBL.name: Tampa Bay Lightning
text: Same old Lightning: 15-5-2, and in the mix again.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 16 of their 22 games.
Expect them to spend most of the night in the other team’s end and get to the dangerous chances.
They stay out of the box and their goaltending has been stealing games.

TOR.name: Toronto Maple Leafs
text: Last season was one to forget in Toronto, and this one hasn’t started much better: they’re 8-13-3, losers of eight straight.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
On the ice, they pounce on turnovers and find a way to get their shots past the blockers.
Their goaltending has let them down and they spend a lot of time in the box.

UTA.name: Utah Mammoth
text: The Mammoth are 11-9-3 so far.
They’ve played better than that record, too, winning the battle for chances more often than not.
Their game? They rarely get stuck out on long shifts and collapse around the net and give up the point.
Their goaltending has let them down.

VAN.name: Vancouver Canucks
text: Last season was one to forget in Vancouver, and this one hasn’t started much better: they’re 5-18-1.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Expect them to crash the net for second chances and spend a lot of the night in their own end.
Their penalty kill leaks and their goaltending has let them down.

VGK.name: Vegas Golden Knights
text: Last spring’s runners-up look hungry: they’re 13-6-5, losers of four straight.
And it’s no mirage: they’ve had the better of the chances in 18 of their 24 games.
Expect them to get in front of a lot of shots and keep the other team to hopeful shots.
They stay out of the box and their penalty kill is airtight.

WSH.name: Washington Capitals
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Capitals are 10-10-0, losers of four straight.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Their game? They get to the dangerous chances and get caught after turnovers too often.

WPG.name: Winnipeg Jets
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Jets are 11-9-3.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
Night to night, they rarely get burned after losing the puck and find a way to get their shots past the blockers.
They create chances even when shorthanded.
